title: The four-point inequality, proved once for every metric space
statement: In any metric space M, d(a,e) <= d(a,b) + d(b,c) + d(c,e). Mathematically this is two applications of the triangle inequality and is of no interest on its own; it is recorded because of WHAT it quantifies over. Its statement begins with a bound variable M ranging over the `Metric` carrier, so it is one of the first two statements in this kernel (with `Metric.dist_self`) that hold of every metric space rather than of one specific carrier. Both instances built so far -- the reals under |x-y| and the Euclidean plane under sqrt(distSq) -- satisfy it without any further proof. That is the property a carrier exists to have, and before the `Metric` record no theorem in the analysis or geometry shelves had it: `CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn`, `CReal.converges_of_cauchy`, the intermediate and extreme value theorems and the whole `CPoint.distSq` development were each proved by hand on one carrier and generalized to nothing.

formal.statement: theorem Metric.dist_quadrilateral : ((x0 : Metric) -> ((x1 : Metric.carrier x0) -> ((x2 : Metric.carrier x0) -> ((x3 : Metric.carrier x0) -> ((x4 : Metric.carrier x0) -> CReal.le (Metric.dist x0 x1 x4) (CReal.add (Metric.dist x0 x1 x2) (CReal.add (Metric.dist x0 x2 x3) (Metric.dist x0 x3 x4))))))))

evidence.supports: Metric.dist_quadrilateral is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.
checkers: producing-build (Kernel::add_declaration, which re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Metric.dist_quadrilateral | grep -cE '^found[[:space:]]+metric[[:space:]]+theorem[[:space:]]+Metric\.dist_quadrilateral[[:space:]]+0$'
evidence.notes: The exit status depends on the finding twice over. kernel_declaration_projection exits NON-ZERO and prints an explanatory error when the named declaration is in no constructed prelude's environment -- asking for a declaration and finding none is a failure there, not an empty answer. grep -c then exits 1 printing 0 if the anchored row is absent or its axiom-footprint column is not 0. Anchored with [[:space:]], never \t: in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t, and 68 fact checkers in this ledger were wrong for exactly that reason. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint/metric, which overflow the default debug thread stack. The `metric` label did not exist in this tool before the commit of record; without it the tool was blind to the prelude, which is indistinguishable from the declaration not existing.

evidence.supports: The triangle-inequality field this theorem consumes is checked, not decorative: rebuilding the reals instance with Metric.CReal.distComm -- a real, admitted theorem of the wrong type -- in the distTriangle slot is REFUSED by Kernel::add_declaration.
checkers: metric::metric_tests, run against a freshly built kernel environment
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib -- metric::metric_tests::the_triangle_field_is_load_bearing --test-threads=4 2>&1 | grep -cE '^test result: ok\. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: The `1 passed` is load-bearing: `cargo test -- <filter>` runs ZERO tests and exits 0 when the filter matches nothing, so a rename would turn this checker green while checking nothing. Requiring the exact count is what makes the exit status depend on the finding. --release is mandatory (the creal/cpoint preludes overflow the debug thread stack); --test-threads=4 keeps the shared build off the OOM ceiling.

provenance.source: Lane `topology-decision`, roadmap W0-3 and W2-1, decided in ADR-1602 (docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1602-the-metric-layer-first-then-pointfree-and-not-open-sets.md). formal.statement is Kernel::render_lean of the declaration's type, taken verbatim from the unfiltered emit of `kernel_declaration_projection`; axiom_footprint is that tool's footprint-size column, which reads Kernel::axiom_footprint.

notes: depends_on is EMPTY and that is a statement, not an omission: the proof uses only the record's own fields (distTriangle twice) plus CReal.add_le_add and CReal.le_trans, and it names no prior fact in this ledger. A reader checking whether the generalization is real should look at the free_symbols line: x0 is a bound variable of type Metric, so the theorem is not about CReal or CPoint at all.
